text: EMERGENCY NON-CONTRAST THORACIC CT EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: PNEUMONIA? TECHNIQUE: 2 mm thick sections were obtained under emergency conditions without intravenous contrast administration. FINDINGS: Since IV contrast was not administered, optimal evaluation of the heart chambers, mediastinal vascular structures, and lymph nodes could not be performed. Heart dimensions are larger than normal. Heart chambers are enlarged. Pericardial effusion was not detected. The trachea and both main bronchi are open. An endotracheal tube was observed in the trachea. Consolidation areas were observed in the upper lobe of the right lung, accompanied by ground-glass opacities including air bronchograms in the lower lobe. Interlobular septal thickenings were observed in the bilateral lower lobes, and passive atelectasis areas were observed in the vicinity of the effusions. Bilateral pleural effusion was observed. ****Signs of pandemic viral infection may not be detected on CT in the early stages. Clinical and laboratory correlation is recommended. In the abdomen, including the section; The left adrenal gland appears thickened.

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: pte? TECHNIQUE: In emergency conditions, 1 mm thick sections were obtained after intravenous contrast agent injection, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: The right anterior chest wall shows a pacemaker and an electrode extending to the heart. The trachea and both main bronchi are of normal width. No significant thrombus was detected in the pulmonary conus, main pulmonary arteries, or other evaluable branches. Heart dimensions are within normal limits. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or either hilum. In the laterobasal segment of the lower lobe of the left lung, areas of centriacinary modular infiltration and infiltrations in a tree-in-bud pattern were observed, consistent with bronchopneumonia. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax.

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: Patient presenting with sudden dyspnea; PTE? Acute pathology? TECHNIQUE: In emergency conditions, 1 mm thick sections were obtained after intravenous contrast agent injection, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: The trachea and both main bronchi are of normal width. Appearances consistent with secretions were noted in the right main bronchus and its branches. The pulmonary conus was measured at 30 mm in diameter, which is borderline. No filling defects consistent with acute PTE were observed in the pulmonary conus or the proximal branches of both main pulmonary arteries. Heart size is slightly enlarged. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. A consolidation area with air bronchograms was observed in the inferior lingular segment of the left lung and the superior segment of the lower lobe of the left lung. In both lungs, nodular infiltrations and ground-glass opacities with centriacinary millimeter-sized confluence tending towards peribronchovascular formation were noted (bronchopneumonic processes?). The described nodular infiltrations were accompanied by focal bronchiectatic changes in places. Peribronchovascular thickening was noted in both lungs. Evaluation in conjunction with the patient's clinical presentation and serology is recommended. A slightly thick-walled pneumocyst with a diameter of 16 mm was noted in the lower lobe of the right lung. Effusion reaching a thickness of 20 mm in the right hemithorax and 3 mm in the left hemithorax, along with compressive atelectasis adjacent to the effusions, were observed. Within the sections; widespread fluid was noted in all recesses of the abdomen. Intense degenerative changes were observed in the bone structures.

EMERGENCY NON-CONTRAST THORACIC CT SCANNING CLINICAL INFORMATION: Right-sided CT scan shows pneumothorax + pneumothorax size? TECHNIQUE: 2 mm thick sections were obtained under emergency conditions without intravenous contrast administration. FINDINGS: Due to the lack of IV contrast, optimal evaluation of the heart chambers, mediastinal vascular structures, and lymph nodes could not be performed. Heart dimensions are normal. No pericardial effusion was detected. Calcified plaques are present in the coronary artery tracts, aorta, and branches. The trachea and both main bronchi are open. An increased number of lymph nodes (LAP) were noted in the mediastinum, the largest measuring 24x19 mm in the right upper paratracheal region. No active infiltration was observed in the lung parenchyma. A 36 mm deep pneumothorax was observed in the right hemithorax, adjacent to the medial segment of the middle lobe. In the right lung, hypodense lesions with soft tissue density were observed at the peribronchovascular level, measuring 40x30 mm, and in the superior segment of the lower lobe, measuring 45x30 mm, with a pleural base and fine fibrotic retraction towards the center (primary lung cancer?). Evaluation of the patient along with their past investigations is recommended. Irregular reticulations consistent with subsegmental atelectasis were observed in the posterobasal segments of the lower lobes of both lungs. A solid nodular lesion causing a pathological fracture was observed in the lateral section of the right 7th rib (metastasis? primary cancer?). Widespread degenerative changes are present in the bone structures. In the abdomen, including the section, a hypodense nodular appearance with a diameter of 38 mm was observed in the middle section of the left kidney (cyst?).

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: PTE? TECHNIQUE: In emergency conditions, 1 mm thick sections were obtained after intravenous contrast agent injection, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: A hypodense nodule measuring 19x13 mm is observed in the left lobe of the thyroid gland. Elective ultrasound control is recommended. The trachea and both main bronchi are of normal width. The imaging was not obtained in the appropriate phase for PTE evaluation. Therefore, the examination is suboptimal. To the extent that could be evaluated, no significant thrombus was detected in the pulmonary conus, main pulmonary arteries, and their evaluable proximal branches. Heart dimensions are within normal limits. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. No active infiltration was observed in the lung parenchyma. Linear fibroatelectatic changes were noted in both lower lobes of the lungs. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax. The gallbladder was not visualized (operated on). Metallic densities indicative of suture materials were observed in the gallbladder lodge. Three to four adjacent lymph nodes, each with a short axis not exceeding 1 cm, were noted in the vicinity of the lesser curvature of the stomach. Endoscopic examination of the stomach is recommended if clinically necessary. Millimetric nodular thickenings were noted in the left adrenal gland. A stepped appearance, suspicious for fracture, was noted in the anterior sections of the 4th and 5th ribs on the right. The described appearances may be related to a previous fracture line.

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: Patient with nausea and vomiting, elevated troponin levels in diabetes mellitus. PTE? Pneumonia? Additional pathology? Additional intra-abdominal pathology? TECHNIQUE: In an emergency setting, 1 mm thick sections were obtained after intravenous contrast agent injection, and evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: Suture materials were noted in the sternum. Calcified plaques were present in the aorta and its branches. Mosaic attenuation was present, more prominent in the lower lobes of both lungs. The trachea and both main bronchi were of normal width. The width of the main mediastinal vascular structures was normal, and no appearance consistent with pulmonary thromboembolism was observed. Heart size was slightly increased. An increased number of lymph nodes in the mediastinum, not reaching pathological size, was noted. A consolidation was observed in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lung, medially, containing air bronchograms and accompanied by a poorly defined ground-glass opacity at the periphery (pneumonic infiltration?). A follow-up examination after treatment is recommended to rule out underlying malignant processes. Irregular, poorly defined ground-glass opacities with bronchovascular involvement were observed in the lingular segment of the left upper lung. This may be significant for atypical infectious processes. Focal linear thickenings were observed in the pleura adjacent to the basal segments of both lower lung lobes. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax.

TECHNIQUE: 2 mm thick sections were obtained under emergency conditions without intravenous contrast administration. FINDINGS: Due to the lack of IV contrast, optimal evaluation of the heart chambers, mediastinal vascular structures, and lymph nodes could not be performed. Heart dimensions are normal. No pericardial effusion was detected. The pulmonary conus measured 36 mm and has an ectatic appearance. The ascending aorta measured 39 mm. Mediastinal and midline structures are displaced to the right. The trachea is open. Numerous pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were observed in the mediastinal lymph node stations, including prevascular, paratracheal, and subcarinal nodes, the largest of which was subcarinal, measuring approximately 41x21 mm. On the right, in the hilar region, although not precisely measurable due to the lack of contrast in the examination, a mass lesion approximately 40x37 mm in size, obliterating the right main bronchus, is observed. In the superior segment of the right lower lung lobe, adjacent to the oblique fissure, a cavitary lesion approximately 56x52 mm in size with a wall approximately 7.5 mm thick is observed. Prominent enhancements consistent with lymphangitic spread are observed in the interstitial structures adjacent to the lesion. In the posterobasal and laterobasal segments of the right lower lung lobe, there are increased densities within the bronchioles, possibly indicative of secretions. Subsegmental atelectasis and fibroatelectatic changes are observed in the lateral segment of the right middle lung lobe. A defective appearance, possibly indicative of a pathological fracture, and a soft tissue density measuring 18x33 mm are observed at this level in the lateral section of the 6th rib on the right. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax. Within the cross-sections, both kidneys appear lobulated in the abdomen, with areas of cortical thinning observed in places. Several stone densities were observed in the pelvicalyceal system of both kidneys, the largest measuring 13 mm in diameter on the right.

EMERGENCY PULMONARY CT ANGIOGRAPHY EXAMINATION CLINICAL INFORMATION: A patient with known essential thrombocytosis and COPD presented with shortness of breath, cough, and fever. PTE? Pneumonia? Effusion? TECHNIQUE: Intravenous contrast agent was injected in an emergency setting, and 1 mm thick sections were obtained. Evaluation was performed in 3 planes using MPR images. 100 ml of nonionic contrast agent was used for the examination. FINDINGS: The trachea and both main bronchi were of normal width. No filling defects consistent with acute PTE were observed in the pulmonary conus, both main pulmonary arteries, and their evaluable proximal branches. Cardiac size was slightly enlarged, predominantly in the right ventricle. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were found in the mediastinum or either hilum. A loss of aeration was noted in the left lung compared to its symmetry, with a loss of aeration and a collapsed consolidated appearance in the apical segment of the upper lobe of the left lung (atelectasis?, consolidation?). Cystic bronchiectatic changes were also observed in this area. Further evaluation, including the patient's history and infection parameters, is recommended. There is retraction in the mediastinum, midline structures, and lung parenchyma towards the apex of the left lung. Fibrotic structures were also noted in the apex of the right lung. Additionally, subsegmental atelectatic changes and thickening in the subpleural space were observed in the lower lobe of the left lung. Furthermore, calcified thickening of the pleura in the paravertebral area of ​​the left hemithorax was noted. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax. Mild degenerative changes were observed in the bone structures. A 25% height loss was noted in the superior endplate of the L1 vertebra.

A follow-up examination after treatment is recommended. No pleural fluid was detected in either hemithorax.

EMERGENCY NON-CONTRAST THORACIC CT SCANNING CLINICAL INFORMATION: Patient presenting with dyspnea. Pneumonia? Effusion? Herniation? (Known diagnosis of herniation following a traffic accident 40 years ago) TECHNIQUE: 2 mm thick sections were obtained under emergency conditions without intravenous contrast administration. FINDINGS: Due to the lack of IV contrast, optimal evaluation of the heart chambers, mediastinal vascular structures, and lymph nodes could not be performed. Heart dimensions are significantly increased. An effusion reaching 3 cm in depth is observed in the pericardial area. Evaluation with echocardiography findings is recommended if necessary. The aortic arch is 3.5 cm, and the pulmonary trunk is 3.8 cm, which is wider than normal. Dense calcified plaques are present in the aortic arch and coronary arteries. A defect in the left hemidiaphragm and herniation of abdominal fat tissue and intestinal loops extending to the lingula and lower lobe in the left hemithorax at the level of the defect are noteworthy. Secondary to this, there is a significant to near-total loss of ventilation in the lingula and lower lobe of the left lung. The trachea and both main bronchi are patent. No active infiltration was observed in the aerated lung parenchyma. Bilateral pleural effusions are present in both hemithoraxes, reaching 3.3 cm on the right at their deepest point. During the examination, deformities were noted posteriorly and laterally in ribs 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 on the left (previous fracture?, previous surgery?). Additionally, there are old fractures in ribs 12 and 11 on the left.

Within the abdominal section, an isodense nodular appearance of 15 mm in diameter is observed in the right kidney (a cyst with dense contents?). Widespread degenerative changes are present in the bone structures. There is scoliosis in the thoracic vertebrae with the opening facing to the left.

Fluid is also present in the oblique fissure on the right. A Bochdalek hernia with herniation of abdominal fat tissue is present in the left half of the diaphragm. Deformities, possibly related to previous fractures, are present in the right 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th ribs and the left 3rd and 10th ribs.

FINDINGS: The examination was evaluated as suboptimal quality secondary to motion artifacts. The trachea and both main bronchi are of normal width. Calcified plaques are present in the coronary artery tracts, aorta, and branches. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. Widespread centriacinar and paraseptal emphysematous changes are present in both lungs, more prominent in the upper lobes. They acquire a panlobular character in the apical segments. Suspected contrast-filling defects are observed in the pulmonary artery branches leading to the lower lobe of the right lung, and a clear distinction between phase-secondary and PTE (Pelvic Thromboepithelial Tetralogy) cannot be made. Evaluation with D-dimer correlation and clinical findings is recommended. Peripherally located irregular reticulations, septal thickenings, and poorly defined ground-glass opacities were observed in the posterior segment of the upper lobe of the right lung and in the dependent sections of both lower lobes of the lungs (sequelae?). A clear distinction regarding infectious processes cannot be made. Plastering-type pleural effusion was observed in both hemithoraxes. Degenerative changes are present in the bone structures.
